sections.h2: Where is Breckinridge County, and what is it like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Breckinridge County stretches along the Ohio River in western Kentucky, facing Perry County, Indiana. At 586 square miles, 567 of them land, it is the biggest of the four counties compared here. Hardinsburg is the seat and the largest city, with Cloverport and Irvington as the other two cities. Grayson, Ohio and Hancock counties adjoin it, and Meade and Hardin lie to the east.

The county was split from Hardin County in 1799 and was the 38th formed in Kentucky. Cloverport once shipped coal oil from the Victoria mines, and Rough River Dam State Resort Park opened up the southern edge in the 1950s. A local-option vote on January 29, 2013 ended 105 years of prohibition, making Breckinridge a wet county.

During the Civil War, Confederate cavalry burned the courthouse while Union troops were using it as a barracks, though most records were saved. Breckinridge County Public Library sits at 308 Old Highway 60 in Hardinsburg, and Saint Romuald Interparochial School is the private school.

Breckinridge runs on Central time, and the Meade and Hardin side to the east keeps Eastern time. A seller lining up a closing with offices across that line should confirm each office's clock.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Breckinridge housing?
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate is 21,503 residents, 5.2 percent above the 2020 count of 20,432, which edges out Bullitt's 5.1 percent for fastest growth among the four. With 35.9 people per square mile, it is also the thinnest settled.

  • An owner's home has a middle value of $156,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owners live in 81.4 percent of housing units, across 8,069 households.
  • Rent in the middle runs $733 a month, and monthly owner costs in the middle are $1,210 with a mortgage and $377 without one.
  • Household income in the middle is $55,843, and 18.3 percent of residents are below the poverty line.
  • Only 14 building permits were issued for 2025, against 10,952 housing units.

At the 2020 count about a quarter of the 10,704 housing units sat vacant, far above Bullitt's share. Few new homes compete with existing ones. Labor force participation among residents 16 and older is 52.6 percent, the average commute is 32.7 minutes, and 283 employers provided 2,480 jobs in 2023, down 0.8 percent from 2022. Retail sales for 2022 were $217.4 million, about $10,370 per resident, and the county counts 1,384 veterans. Broadband reaches 83.9 percent of households, a point to raise when buyers work remotely.

sections.h2: Which Breckinridge County office does what?
sections.html:
The sheriff bills and collects, the PVA values property, and the county clerk takes over unpaid bills. The Sheriff's Office is at 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, open weekdays eight to four Central. The phone is 270-756-2361 and the mailing box is PO Box 127. It collects about $11 million a year on behalf of the state, county, schools and special districts.

Assessment and homestead questions go to the PVA at 270-756-5154. Past-due real estate bills go to the County Clerk (270-756-2246), who quotes payoff amounts.

sections.h2: What are the Breckinridge County tax payment dates?
sections.html:
For the 2026 bills the sheriff said mailing would finish by October 29, and an owner without a bill by November 10 should ask for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment run from November 1 through 4 p.m. Central on April 15. Postmarks count.

Breckinridge County Sheriff's payment stages on the 2026 bills
WindowAmount owed
November 1 to 30Face amount less 2%
December 1 to 31Face amount
January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21%
After April 15Pay at the County Clerk's office

Statute and the Revenue Cabinet fix these dates and percentages, and the sheriff cannot bend them.

sections.h2: How does paying a Breckinridge County bill work?
sections.html:
The sheriff takes only the exact amount printed on the bill. A short payment is mailed back, and installments are not offered. One payment may cover several bills.

  • Online: a processing fee of 1.5 percent, minimum $1.50, applies on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on anything over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck work.
  • Mail or counter: a check or money order with the voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form has to accompany the payment, so owners opting out pay by mail or at the counter.

Your cancelled check is the receipt, or enclose a stamped, addressed envelope for a mailed one.

sections.h2: How are taxes split when a Breckinridge County house sells?
sections.html:
The bill is made out to whoever owned on January 1. Selling after that date still leaves the bill in your name, and you pass it to the new owner. The closing agent usually allocates each side's portion on the settlement statement.

The sheriff will not accept two prorated checks. One party or the other has to pay the full bill, so ask the closing attorney who carries the payment and whether the buyer gets a credit.

sections.h2: How can a Breckinridge County owner dispute a valuation?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1, and the PVA's crews revisit every property about once in four years. If a new value seems wrong, schedule a conference with the PVA while the roll is open to inspection, which begins in early May and lasts thirteen days.

Only after that conference can you file with the county clerk, who serves as clerk to the local appeals board. The board meets about a month after inspection closes. Bring photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or comparable sales, since boards decide on paper and an appeal without it is denied.

sections.h2: Is there a senior or disability break in Breckinridge County?
sections.html: Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classed as totally disabled, may claim the homestead exemption on the house they live in, up to $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. About 21.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 92.5 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. The sheriff sends every exemption question to the PVA, and says that checking for an exemption is the first move when a bill feels heavy.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Breckinridge County property tax?
sections.html: The sheriff treats a bill as delinquent after April 15, or after the tax day assigned for that year, and extra penalties may apply. After April 15 the sheriff drops the bill and it shows up at the clerk as delinquent, with a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions for the clerk and county attorney follow, and notices and advertising come before any sale. The Department of Revenue posts each county's delinquent list online by June 1, and on a normal schedule a sale can fall between July 14 and August 28. A third party can buy a bill that reaches the sale list. Anyone selling a house here with old tax owing should order the payoff before closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

faqs.q: What is the Breckinridge County sheriff's tax office address?
faqs.a: 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Payments by mail go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, starting November 1. A convenience fee applies, and the payment must equal the exact bill amount.

faqs.q: Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff accepts the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

faqs.q: When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?
faqs.a: On February 1, and it runs through April 15. After that the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed. The closing agent usually prorates the year, but the sheriff still needs the whole bill paid at once.
